composition:
  authorize: "hasRole('OWNER_ADMIN')"

# Replay an already-seen Idempotency-Key as the original owner (200) before creating again.
checkIdempotency:
  class: org.springframework.samples.petclinic.rest.function.owner.CheckIdempotencyKey
  govern: [ transaction ]
  next: build

build:
  class: org.springframework.samples.petclinic.rest.function.owner.BuildOwner
  govern: [ transaction ]
  next: checkEmailDomain

# Reject a disposable-mail-provider email domain with 400 before any persistence.
checkEmailDomain:
  class: org.springframework.samples.petclinic.rest.function.owner.CheckEmailDomain
  govern: [ transaction ]
  next: validatePostcode

# Validate an optional postcode against the city's region before any persistence.
validatePostcode:
  class: org.springframework.samples.petclinic.rest.function.owner.ValidatePostcode
  govern: [ transaction ]
  next: assignHousehold

# Assign householdId before the identity check so it forms part of the key. Household
# members with different telephones are admitted here and capped by MembershipLevel; the
# identity check below is the sole duplicate gate (see CheckUniqueIdentity).
assignHousehold:
  class: org.springframework.samples.petclinic.rest.function.owner.AssignHouseholdId
  govern: [ transaction ]
  next: checkIdentity

checkIdentity:
  class: org.springframework.samples.petclinic.rest.function.owner.CheckUniqueIdentity
  method: service
  govern: [ transaction ]
  next: checkCityCapacity

checkCityCapacity:
  class: org.springframework.samples.petclinic.rest.function.owner.CheckCityCapacity
  govern: [ transaction ]
  next: adjustDate

adjustDate:
  class: org.springframework.samples.petclinic.rest.function.owner.AdjustRegistrationDate
  govern: [ transaction ]
  next: checkDailyLimit

checkDailyLimit:
  class: org.springframework.samples.petclinic.rest.function.owner.CheckDailyLimit
  govern: [ transaction ]
  next: assignCode

assignCode:
  class: org.springframework.samples.petclinic.rest.function.owner.AssignCustomerCode
  govern: [ transaction ]
  next: dedupeCode

# De-duplicate the assigned customerCode against existing owners: append '-<n>' with the
# smallest n >= 2 on collision, before the code is persisted.
dedupeCode:
  class: org.springframework.samples.petclinic.rest.function.owner.DeduplicateCustomerCode
  govern: [ transaction ]
  next: countNamesakes

countNamesakes:
  class: org.springframework.samples.petclinic.rest.function.owner.AssignNamesakeCount
  govern: [ transaction ]
  next: flagBulkSignup

flagBulkSignup:
  class: org.springframework.samples.petclinic.rest.function.owner.FlagBulkSignup
  govern: [ transaction ]
  next: flagPossibleDuplicate

flagPossibleDuplicate:
  class: org.springframework.samples.petclinic.rest.function.owner.FlagPossibleDuplicate
  govern: [ transaction ]
  next: save

save:
  class: org.springframework.samples.petclinic.rest.function.owner.SaveOwner
  govern: [ transaction ]
  next: recordIdempotency

# Remember the new owner under its Idempotency-Key so a repeat replays it instead of duplicating.
recordIdempotency:
  class: org.springframework.samples.petclinic.rest.function.owner.RecordIdempotencyKey
  govern: [ transaction ]
  next: audit

audit:
  class: org.springframework.samples.petclinic.rest.function.owner.AuditOwnerCreated
  govern: [ transaction ]
  next: respond

respond:
  class: org.springframework.samples.petclinic.rest.function.owner.RespondWithOwnerCreated
  govern: [ transaction ]

`AcceptanceTest` is the only test class, and all its tests pass. The change is complete.

## Summary

I redesigned the identity key and duplicate detection as specified, keeping structural impact low: **3 files touched**, one new small class, and only `static` helper methods changed (each `service` orchestration method left untouched).

**`Soundex.java` (new)** — a small, cohesive utility (`code` + a private `digit` lookup) producing the American Soundex code of a surname. Shared by both the identity key and the soft-match, so the phonetic logic lives in one place.

**`CheckUniqueIdentity.java`** — rewrote only the static `identityKey(owner)` helper (plus three tiny private helpers) so the key is now `SHA-256 hex over (normalizedTelephone + '|' + lowerEmail + '|' + soundex(lastName))`. The `service` method (the 409 gate) is unchanged, so it still ignores deleted owners and self, and the POST pipeline still runs the email-domain blocklist (`CheckEmailDomain`) before it. The mapper's `identityKey` expression needed no change since the signature is preserved — the response now exposes the 64-hex key.

**`FlagPossibleDuplicate.java`** — the soft match now fires when `identityKey` differs but `soundex(lastName)` and `postcode` match (dropping the old normalized-lastName + different-telephone check and the now-unused `equalsTelephone` helper).

Behavioural consequences, all satisfied:
- Telephone is part of the key, so two owners with the same last name and postcode but **different telephones** are no longer a hard duplicate — they're created and flagged as a soft match.
- The former household-duplicate 409 (`CheckUniqueHousehold`) was already not wired into `owners.POST.yml`; identity is now the single duplicate gate, and `householdId` no longer participates in the key (it's still assigned for tier/ceiling rules).

`AcceptanceTest` (both tests — 64-hex key shape and identical-identity → 409) passes; `BUILD SUCCESS`.
